title: Make Ctrl+C and Escape reliable through the interactive VM PTY path
objective: Part of integration ticket #66. Diagnose owner-reported intermittent Ctrl+C/Escape in the complete terminal→public launcher→SSH/PTTY→tmux→OpenCode path, then fix the demonstrated layer without weakening clipboard or host security protections.

acceptance_criteria.text: A source-backed behavior matrix distinguishes Ctrl+C/Escape in ordinary prompt entry, active generation, the exit-confirm modal and other menus; unspecified OpenCode contexts are not assigned invented semantics.
The full interactive path reliably delivers the intended keys/signals and preserves normal local-terminal-like input, output, resize, reattach and session behavior.
Regression coverage exercises actual PTYs and the relevant launcher/SSH/tmux boundary, not only mocked key handlers; failures produce bounded actionable diagnostics.
Existing SSH restrictions, tmux/session identity, terminal clipboard protections and host security boundary remain intact; EscapeChar=none is not treated as an OSC-52 defense.

The public helper request protocol does not consume terminal input: it reads bounded JSON first, then reopens the controlling TTY for the interactive client, preserves foreground process group and stdin/stdout/stderr, resize/signals, and returns the exact SSH exit status. Profile private keys are read only from their canonical protected paths, never staged in a workspace or generic temp directory, and strict guest host-key pinning is used without TOFU.

needed: Reproduce repeated key cases through a controlling PTY at the supported pinned OpenCode binary and distinguish bytes from SIGINT at each PTY boundary.
Cover generation, ordinary prompt, exit-confirm cancel/confirm and supported menu behavior; test SSH disconnect/tmux reattach.
Add actual-PTY regression for the production interactive wrapper and retain existing key-binding unit coverage.
Owner performs final interactive Ariadne validation and clipboard canary under the documented safe terminal configuration.

Production-helper PTY test sends the JSON request separately from keystrokes typed after SSH starts; assert controlling TTY/foreground group, real input bytes, resize, Ctrl+C, exact exit status and non-TTY refusal. Verify no secret key bytes in argv/env/logs/temp/workspace and strict guest host-key pinning before first SSH.
created: scripts/verify-exit-confirm.py --via-launcher: production guest launcher template, pre-existing tmux 500 ms repair, PTY resize and exit-confirm flow
cases: Owner reports OpenCode TUI is operational on Ariadne but Ctrl+C/Escape behavior is intermittent. Exact failing context/key sequence and underlying cause are not yet established.

Sol Medium design review (2026-11-24): PASS at design level for the shared VM profile/runtime/CLI integration baseline in docs/vm-usability-integration.md and docs/systemd-vm.md; owner authorized implementation. This is design approval only, not implementation, test, security, host-validation, acceptance-criterion, or owner-acceptance evidence.
verify-exit-confirm.py --via-launcher: launcher resets escape-time 500 ms → 10 ms; 10/10 fast Escape+n cancellation trials; resize and detach/reattach pass on OpenCode 2.2.5
